reviews.author: Gregory (Meta)
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the implementation of for_each_node_mask_state() uses the bitmap intersection helpers, but this may not be efficient for large node masks or states, and requested a benchmark to verify its performance.
reviews.raw_body:
Add first_node_state() and next_node_state(), so callers can walk any
node state the way first_memory_node and next_memory_node walk N_MEMORY.

Add for_each_node_mask_state(), which iterates a nodemask intersected
with a node state using the bitmap intersection helpers, without a
temporary nodemask.

Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
---
 include/linux/nodemask.h | 17 +++++++++++++++++
 1 file changed, 17 insertions(+)

diff --git a/include/linux/nodemask.h b/include/linux/nodemask.h
index 607373bd83ee..90bdcffa42ea 100644
--- a/include/linux/nodemask.h
+++ b/include/linux/nodemask.h
@@ -411,6 +411,11 @@ enum node_states {
 
 extern nodemask_t node_states[NR_NODE_STATES];
 
+/* Iterate the nodes in a mask that also belong to the specified state. */
+#define for_each_node_mask_state(node, mask, state)			\
+	for_each_and_bit(node, nodes_addr(mask),			\
+			 nodes_addr(node_states[state]), MAX_NUMNODES)
+
 #if MAX_NUMNODES > 1
 static __always_inline int node_state(int node, enum node_states state)
 {
@@ -435,6 +440,12 @@ static __always_inline int num_node_state(enum node_states state)
 #define for_each_node_state(__node, __state) \
 	for_each_node_mask((__node), node_states[__state])
 
+#define first_node_state(state)	first_node(node_states[state])
+static __always_inline unsigned int next_node_state(int nid, enum node_states state)
+{
+	return next_node(nid, node_states[state]);
+}
+
 #define first_online_node	first_node(node_states[N_ONLINE])
 #define first_memory_node	first_node(node_states[N_MEMORY])
 static __always_inline unsigned int next_online_node(int nid)
@@ -481,6 +492,12 @@ static __always_inline int num_node_state(enum node_states state)
 #define for_each_node_state(node, __state) \
 	for ( (node) = 0; (node) == 0; (node) = 1)
 
+#define first_node_state(state)	0
+static __always_inline unsigned int next_node_state(int nid, enum node_states state)
+{
+	return MAX_NUMNODES;
+}
+
 #define first_online_node	0
 #define first_memory_node	0
 #define next_online_node(nid)	(MAX_NUMNODES)

-- 
2.56.1

2026-11-20.patch_summary: This patch adds functionality to iterate over nodes that belong to a specific state, such as online or memory nodes. It introduces two new functions: first_node_state() and next_node_state(), which allow callers to walk through the nodes in a particular state. Additionally, it defines for_each_node_mask_state(), which intersects a nodemask with a node state using bitmap helpers without creating a temporary nodemask. This patch aims to simplify and improve the way node states are iterated over in the Linux kernel.

reviews.author: Yury Norov
reviews.summary:
Reviewer Yury Norov noted that the new function name for_each_node_mask_state() is inconsistent with existing functions, suggesting a more consistent naming convention and asking if other similar helpers were considered.

Reviewer Yury Norov noted that only a subset of node-state iterators were converted to use the new helpers, and requested a thorough check to ensure all relevant functions have been updated.
reviews.raw_body:
for_each_node_state_and? We've got for_each_node(), and we've got
for_each_node_state(), so let's figure out consistent naming.

Did you check the codebase for exsisting candidates for this helper?

---

At least the following {first,next}_{online,memory}_node must be
switched to the new helpers. Can you check through the rest of the
kernel to make sure all candidates of the proposed helpers are
converted?

reviews.author: Gregory (Meta)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer suggested changing for_each_node_mask_state() to use for_each_node_mask_and() for consistency, requiring only a simple replacement of N_MEMORY with N_MEMORY_X

Reviewer Gregory noted that the patch's use of MAX_NUMNODES in for_each_node_mask_state() may be incorrect, and suggested verifying its correctness by comparing it to the actual number of nodes.

Reviewer Gregory (Meta) noted that the original intention was to remove first/next_memory_node, but it was left in to save an extra patch; he suggested updating the current implementation instead.
reviews.raw_body:
for_each_node_mask_and() would be more consistent, change just requires
passing node_state[N_MEMORY_X] instead of just the node state bit.

---

I followed for_each_node_mask() which uses MAX_NUMANODES but let me
look.

---

I originally intended to delete first/next_memory_node, to make
usage of N_MEMORY a bit more obviously, but dropped it to save an
extra patch or two.  I will probably add that back in.

But yeah i can update these otherwise.

-- 
~Gregory
